brief: An invented bicycle rental shop (synthetic example). Customers rent bicycles by the hour. Staff check each bicycle out and back in and record damage. A manager must approve any refund above 50 euros.

items.name: Bicycle

value.description: A bicycle in the shop's rental fleet.

items.rationale: The brief says bicycles are rented and checked out and in. The states are inferred from check-out, check-in and damage recording.

items.name: Rental

value.description: One hourly rental of one bicycle by one customer, from check-out to check-in.

items.rationale: The brief says rental is by the hour and that staff check bicycles out and in. The states and amount attributes are inferred.

items.name: DamageReport

value.description: A record of damage found on a bicycle, made by staff.

items.rationale: The brief says staff record damage. The states are inferred.

items.name: Refund

value.description: Money returned to a customer for a rental.

items.rationale: The brief requires manager approval for refunds above 50 euros, so refunds must carry an amount and an approval status. The states are inferred.
Each rental concerns a bicycle that is checked out and back in. The assumption is one bicycle per rental.
Damage is recorded on bicycles.
Damage is recorded at check-in, which links it to a rental.
The assumption is that refunds relate to a rental. The brief does not say so.

items.name: check_out_bicycle

value.description: Staff hand an available bicycle to a customer and start the hourly rental.

items.rationale: The brief says staff check each bicycle out.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: check_in_bicycle

value.description: Staff take back a bicycle and end the rental.

items.rationale: The brief says staff check each bicycle back in.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: record_damage

value.description: Staff record damage found on a bicycle.

items.rationale: The brief says staff record damage. Marking the bicycle as damaged is inferred.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: request_refund

value.description: Create a refund request for a rental.

items.rationale: Refunds exist per the brief. A request step is inferred so that approval can happen before payment.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: approve_refund

value.description: A manager approves a refund request.

items.rationale: The brief says a manager must approve any refund above 50 euros.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: reject_refund

value.description: A manager rejects a refund request.

items.rationale: Inferred counterpart to approval.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: issue_refund

value.description: Pay the refund back to the customer.

items.rationale: Refunds of 50 euros or less need no approval according to the brief. Larger refunds must be approved first.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: R1

value.description: Any refund above 50 euros must be approved by a manager before it is issued.

items.rationale: Stated directly in the brief. It concerns customers' money beyond a stated limit, so a person decides.

items.name: R2

value.description: A refund above 50 euros may not be issued unless it has been approved.

items.rationale: An engine-checkable guard that enforces R1.

items.name: R3

value.description: Only staff (or managers) may check bicycles out and in and record damage.

items.rationale: The brief assigns check-out, check-in and damage recording to staff. The same access applies to check_in_bicycle and record_damage. Including managers is inferred.

items.name: R4

value.description: Only managers may approve or reject refunds.

items.rationale: The brief says the manager approves refunds above 50 euros. The same access applies to reject_refund.

items.name: R5

value.description: Damage must be checked and recorded, if present, when a bicycle is checked in, before the rental is closed.

items.rationale: Inferred from staff recording damage at check-in. The ordering relative to refunds is not stated in the brief.

rejected.problem: invalid expression '100% of rentals reach status returned with damage assessed': invalid syntax

rejected.name: Customer
rejected.problem: entity 'Customer' must declare at least one state

questions.question: Is the 50-euro limit per refund, or cumulative per rental or customer? And does a refund of exactly 50 euros need approval?
questions.why: Rule R1 depends on how the threshold applies. The brief says 'above 50', which is read as strictly greater than 50.

questions.question: Why are refunds given (early return, bicycle fault, overcharge), and who may request one?
questions.why: This determines when request_refund may happen and whether refunds always relate to a rental.

questions.question: Is the customer charged for recorded damage, and if so who decides the amount and is there a limit that needs manager review?
questions.why: Damage charges affect customers' money. The brief records damage but says nothing about charging for it.

questions.question: Can a damaged bicycle be rented again, and who clears it back to available?
questions.why: This decides whether check_out_bicycle must be blocked for damaged bicycles and what happens after a damage report.

questions.question: Can one rental include several bicycles, and how are hours rounded and priced?
questions.why: This affects the cardinality of Rental to Bicycle and how the rental amount is computed.

questions.question: Which systems are used today (point of sale, payment terminal, fleet list)?
questions.why: Needed to describe the integrations for refund payment and rental records.

roles.name: Staff
roles.description: Shop employees who check bicycles out and in, record damage and may request refunds.

roles.name: Manager
roles.description: Approves or rejects refunds above 50 euros. May also perform staff tasks.

roles.name: Customer
roles.description: Rents bicycles by the hour. External party, with no system role assumed.

agents.name: rental_desk_assistant
agents.description: Helps staff record check-outs, check-ins and damage reports, and prepares refund requests. It never approves refunds above 50 euros.

agents.name: refund_processor
agents.description: Issues refunds of 50 euros or less, and larger refunds only after a manager has approved them.

integrations.system: Payment terminal / payment provider (to be confirmed)
integrations.description: Pays refunds back to the customer's payment method.

integrations.system: Point-of-sale or rental register (to be confirmed)
integrations.description: Records rental start and bicycle assignment. The same system would also serve rental.check_in.

suggestions.note: descriptions only: roles are granted and systems are connected by an administrator

assumptions.statement: A refund 'above 50 euros' means Refund.amount > 50, so refunds of 50 euros or less can be issued without a manager.
Each rental involves one customer and one bicycle.
Refunds relate to a specific rental.
Damage is recorded at check-in and a damaged bicycle is not rented out until cleared.

unknowns: Hourly rate, rounding rules and any deposit
Reasons for and initiators of refunds
Whether damage leads to customer charges, and who decides them
Process and owner for returning a damaged bicycle to service
What happens with late or missing returns
Payment and point-of-sale systems in use

understanding.summary: A synthetic bicycle rental shop rents bicycles to customers by the hour. Staff check each bicycle out and back in and record any damage. Any refund above 50 euros needs a manager's approval.
understanding.outcome: Rentals are tracked from check-out to check-in, damage is recorded, and refunds above 50 euros are released only after a manager approves them.
out_of_scope: Pricing and tariff management beyond the hourly basis
Reservations or booking ahead (not mentioned in the brief)
